President Trump’s willingness to consider Article 5-like security guarantees for Ukraine is a critical feature to achieving lasting peace. Russia’s willingness to discuss such guarantees is a major step forward and potential indication that it is serious about peace.

A credible Article 5-like guarantee, backed by deterrence and deconfliction arrangements, could dramatically reduce the risk of another war. President Zelensky is right that these guarantees must be specific, credible, and clearly documented. That is exactly the work @SEPeaceMissions and I are undertaking together.

These are among the most significant commitments the United States can make and require careful consideration.

@realDonaldTrump would have to approve any proposed guarantee, subject to constitutional and congressional processes. He would take such a step only if he believed it clearly served America’s national interests and the broader security arrangements made it highly unlikely that the guarantee would ever be invoked.

This is why security guarantees for Ukraine cannot be finalized in isolation from post-war European security architecture. The two must be considered together.

European security institutions and agreements provide an important foundation. Our objective is to strengthen them, identify where existing mechanisms failed to prevent this war, and develop more effective arrangements to reduce future conflict.

That includes permanent channels for consultation, crisis communication, military deconfliction, greater transparency, and reciprocal measures to reduce escalation. We need clear understandings of the intentions and commitments of all parties, and practical mechanisms that function even during serious disagreement.

We seek a future where Ukraine is secure, Europe is stronger, Russia has confidence that NATO is not seeking confrontation, and NATO and its partners have confidence that Russia will respect the sovereignty and security of its neighbors. This requires clear statements of intent, supported by credible, verifiable commitments. Any framework must preserve the sovereignty and independent decision-making of all participating nations.

Security must also be supported by economic strength. Ukraine needs a credible long-term prosperity plan, with reforms that strengthen its institutions, economy, and self-reliance. The substantial commitments by America and Europe must be matched by Ukraine’s commitment to its own success.

Over the coming weeks, in private conversations and multilateral discussions, we intend to work with Ukraine, our European partners, and Russia to try and reach a common understanding on this architecture.

If we can develop a framework with clear commitments, reciprocal obligations, and credible implementation, it will give us greater confidence that everyone is prepared to take the steps necessary for peace.

Nothing is agreed until it is agreed. But the willingness to engage on these historic questions creates an important opportunity to stop the bloodshed.

As President Trump emphasized in his conversation with the Coalition of the Willing leaders, the hundreds of billions currently being spent on this war could instead be invested in our economies—creating jobs, driving growth, lowering energy prices, and strengthening infrastructure.

Our goal is a sovereign, secure, prosperous and free Ukraine, a stronger and more stable Europe, and a lasting peace built on arrangements that make another war far less likely.

That is the work ahead of us.

Russia attacks civilian areas across Ukraine, killing and injuring people in their homes, shops, and other everyday places.

Yesterday in Dymer, Kyiv region, a Russian drone destroyed part of a five-storey apartment building. At least 11 people were killed. Rescuers worked through the day and night, pulling survivors from the rubble, including 7-year-old Davyd, who had been trapped for almost 14 hours, and an elderly woman, Valentyna, rescued after 22 hours.

In another part of the Kyiv region, a Russian strike on a supermarket killed three people and injured 13. In Kharkiv, Russian drones struck an educational facility and a hotel, injuring eight people. In Sumy region, an FPV drone targeted a vehicle delivering bread and other food supplies to residents.

These attacks show why Ukraine urgently needs stronger air defence, including more anti-ballistic interceptors, to protect civilian lives.

Doctors are now providing the necessary care to Davyd, the boy who was rescued from the rubble of a building in Dymer yesterday. His parents are with him now. Four other people who were injured are also in hospital. Among them is a woman who was rescued overnight after spending almost 22 hours under the rubble.

Clearing the rubble at the site continued throughout the night. Unfortunately, the bodies of seven more people killed were recovered from the rubble. In total, this single Russian strike killed 11 people. My condolences to all their relatives and loved ones... The fate of two people remains unknown. The production of these “Shaheds”—both conventional and jet-powered—which Russia uses to destroy residential buildings and infrastructure in Ukraine, is critically dependent on foreign components, primarily the supply of engines and chips to Russia. Global sanctions, monitoring compliance with sanctions regimes, and genuinely strengthening export controls are what can limit Russian weapons production. Every country and every leader who helps put pressure on the aggressor also helps protect lives. It is important to remember this and take action—to act so that there is less Russian weaponry and it becomes harder to produce. Thank you to everyone who stands with Ukraine!

Зараз лікарі надають необхідну допомогу Давиду – хлопчику, якого вчора врятували з-під завалів будинку в Димері. Батьки зараз перебувають поруч із ним. Ще четверо людей, які були поранені, також перебувають в лікарні. Серед них і жінка, яку вночі вдалося врятувати, вона пробула під завалами майже 22 години.

Розбір завалів на місці тривав усю ніч. З-під завалів дістали, на жаль, ще тіла семи загиблих. Загалом тільки одним цим російським ударом вбито 11 людей. Мої співчуття всім рідним та близьким... Доля двох людей досі невідома. Порятунок та пошук людей доводилось переривати через загрозу повторних російських ударів і небезпеку від «шахедів».

Виробництво таких «шахедів» – і звичайних, і реактивних, – якими Росія розбиває житлові будинки та інфраструктуру в Україні, критично залежне від іноземних компонентів, передусім від постачання в Росію двигунів та чипів. Санкції світу, контроль за дотриманням санкційних режимів і реальне посилення експортного контролю – це те, що може обмежити російське виробництво зброї. Кожна країна, кожен лідер, які допомагають тиску на агресора, допомагають і захисту життя. Важливо про це пам’ятати і діяти – діяти так, щоб російської зброї було менше і щоб виробляти її було складніше. Дякую всім, хто з Україною!
